key_insight: Using a reverse predictivity measure, the authors show that only a subset of artificial neural network units meaningfully align with primate brain responses, revealing substantial ANN–brain misalignment compared with strong bidirectional alignment between two primate brains.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of bidirectional, unit-level evaluation of correspondence between ANN activity and biological neural responses, exposing hidden mismatches that standard forward predictivity metrics miss.
method: Introduce and compute reverse predictivity (brain→ANN) in addition to standard forward predictivity (ANN→brain) to assess bidirectional alignment.
Compare predictivity distributions across individual ANN units and primate neurons using neural recordings and model activations to identify which ANN units align.
Quantify and contrast ANN–brain alignment with brain–brain alignment to reveal the extent and nature of misalignment.
impact: Highlights that surface-level ANN–brain similarity can mask unit-level mismatches, pushing ML practitioners to adopt bidirectional, unit-resolved evaluation for model selection, interpretation, and brain-inspired design.
visual_elements: Bidirectional schematic: arrows between ANN and brain showing forward (ANN→brain) vs reverse (brain→ANN) predictivity.
Distribution plots: side-by-side histograms/violin plots comparing predictivity scores for ANN units vs primate neurons.
Unit-level heatmap: matrix showing which ANN units are aligned (high reverse predictivity) and which are not.
Scatter plot: per-unit forward vs reverse predictivity to highlight aligned subset and misaligned population.
paper_title: Reverse predictivity for bidirectional comparison of neural networks and biological brains
